title.narrative: Emergency Response to Drought and Natural Disasters and Improvement of Socio-economic Conditions for Host and Refugee Communities

description.narrative: Kalobeyei Settlement has hosted increasing refugee-host populations for more than twenty years – in the last two years, there has seen an increase of 15.6% from 38,081 to 45,122, with the settlement population rapidly expanding. The Advisory Settlement Development Plan formulated by UN-Habitat in 2017-2018 anticipates a total population of 60,000, and with rapid population increase, existing public infrastructures will struggle to cope. Over the last two years, Turkana has experienced dire humanitarian-climate change catastrophes such as severe droughts (27% of rainfall during Oct’21 to Mar’22) and flooding of unpredictable natures (180% of rainfall during Dec’20-May’21 at 180% and May’22 at 192%, and possibility of El Nino effect upcoming). From experience, there are high risks of flash floods emerging after extended droughts which can displace communities resulting in large loss of lives, as well as destruction of public facilities. These vulnerabilities are exacerbated by crop failure and water scarcity compounded by the global economic crisis from the combined impact of the Covid-19 pandemic and the war in Ukraine. The pandemic has devastated the existing economy with many refugees and host members losing income and livelihood opportunities and has also spread health risks to refugees and hosts who have insufficient access to health and basic services, increasing overall tensions and conflicts within the region. This requires urgent interventions to ensure communities are food secure improve disaster preparedness and response, rehabilitate land for better efficient use, provide adequate infrastructures and build capacity for resilience
